title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from p.43: S is a set with a topology τ. T ⊂ S is τ-closed and U = S∖T is its open complement. On T a topology τ'_0 is given. The argument on p.43 needs τ'_0 to be finer than τ|T, though the text does not state this explicitly.

Definition of τ'. Its closed sets are the X ⊂ S of the form X = B ∪ cl_τ(X∩U), with B closed in (T, τ'_0). Page 43 shows that τ' belongs to a class C of topologies τ'' with these properties: τ'' is finer than τ, τ''|U = τ|U, τ''|T = τ'_0, and T is τ''-closed. It also shows that τ' is the least fine (coarsest) member of C. This is a 'recollement' in which the topology on the closed piece T is refined while the open piece U and the attaching data are kept.

Item d) is about specialization preorders. The only nontrivial case is x ∈ T, y ∈ U. That case reduces to showing that the τ'-closure of {y}, or more generally of any Y ⊂ U, equals its τ-closure. A priori the τ'-closure is the larger one; the text says 'smaller', but closure under a finer topology is smaller, so the text is right.

Corollary on this page: for X ⊂ U, cl_τ'(X) = cl_τ(X). Proof: let X' ⊇ A be τ'-closed. By conditions 1°–3°, X' ⊇ cl_τ(X'∩U) ⊇ cl_τ(A). Hence cl_τ'(A) ⊇ cl_τ(A); the reverse inclusion holds because τ' is finer.

Marginal general formula: for any X ⊂ S, cl_τ'(X) = cl_τ(X∩U) ∪ cl_τ'_0(X∩T). The first term is τ-closed, hence τ'-closed. The second is closed in T and T is τ'-closed, so it is τ'-closed. The union contains X and is clearly minimal. The formula is reused on p.45.

Item e) begins here. There are maps of spaces I' → I with a saturation map p, and the claim is that the topology of I is induced/quotient in a suitable sense. A p-saturated subset p^{-1}(A) is closed for the tilde topology iff it is closed for τ' and its trace (on T) is closed for τ. Page 45 rephrases this as an initial-topology statement: τ on S is the initial topology for id: S → (S, τ') together with i: T → S.

Purpose: elementary point-set lemmas for gluing and modifying topologies along an open/closed decomposition, presumably for 'figures' (stratified or constructible objects) in the 'Algèbre des figures' chapter.
errors: The hypothesis that τ'_0 is finer than τ|T is used implicitly (so that cl_τ(X∩U)∩T is τ'_0-closed) but is never stated on these pages.
In the corollary's proof the letter X is reused for the closed set containing A, which clashes with X ⊂ U in the statement. This is notational only; the argument is correct.

The roles of τ and τ' in e) and on p.45 seem swapped relative to p.43–44, judging from the transcription. Some hesitation or inconsistency in notation is visible, but no mathematical error is evident.

ideas.what: Coarsest topology refining τ, agreeing with τ on the open part U and with a prescribed finer topology on the closed part T, with T kept closed (re-gluing along an open/closed decomposition)
ideas.modern_name: recollement / Artin gluing of topologies (open–closed decomposition)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin gluing; recollement formalized in SGA4 (Artin–Grothendieck–Verdier) and BBD for sheaves
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exp. IV §9 (recollement of topoi), in the topos setting

ideas.what: Closure formula cl_τ'(X) = cl_τ(X∩U) ∪ cl_τ'_0(X∩T), and the fact that closures of subsets of U are unchanged
ideas.modern_name: closure operator for a glued topology

ideas.what: Characterization of closed saturated sets via τ' and the trace on T (initial topology for S→(S,τ') and T→S)
ideas.modern_name: initial/final topology characterization of a glued space

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine point-set verifications about gluing topologies along a closed subset. They are correct, standard, and serve as auxiliary lemmas in an unpublished chapter.
transcription_corrections: 'X ⊃ A, fermé pour τ'' — the X here is a τ'-closed set containing A, not the X ⊂ U of the corollary.
The margin formula reads cl^{(τ')}(X) = cl^{(τ)}(X∩U) ∪ cl^{(τ'_0)}(X∩T). The second closure is taken in T for τ'_0, as p.45 confirms.
'(a priori la première serait plus petite)' refers to the τ'-closure being a priori smaller, since τ' is finer.
